title: Approval entropy mitigation - PRD brain dump
content:
Purpose:
This is a messy working draft describing an approach to reduce approval "entropy" across Private deployments by: 1) making approval evidence compact & verifiable, 2) bounding retention/ingest cost in customer-managed networking scenarios, and 3) adding observable signals so operators can detect noisy/meaningless approvals before they affect audits and rollbacks.

Context / motivation:
- Customers using Private deployments often have high-volume network events (ephemeral host changes, NAT translations, managed firewall rules) that create heavy churn in approval systems and audit logs.
- We see two failure modes: (a) audit bloat: enormous retention bills + poor UX for reviewers, and (b) approval signal degradation: too-many-approvals for low-risk changes mask real risky events.
- Goal: preserve forensic value while reducing cost and surfacing high-signal approvals.

High-level proposal (three pillars):
1) Compact evidence + canonical event bundle (CEB): canonicalize multi-step change sequences into a single signed bundle with summary + compact diffs.
2) Risk-scored gate with sampling: run a lightweight policy that classifies changes by risk (low/medium/high) and applies different approval/retention policies.
3) Telemetry-derived sentinel triggers: detect abnormal patterns (burst approvals, repeated equivalent approvals, operator churn) and surface these as MTL (must-track) alerts to SRE and customer-ops.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not attempt to redesign customer-side network provisioning tools.
- Not aiming to notarize every packet or replace SIEMs — we must interop, not compete.

Detailed requirements:
- Functional:
  - event schema for CEB: timestamp, actor-id, actor-role (customer/operator/redwood), action-type, resource-path, compact-diff (base64 gzip), preimage-hash, postimage-hash, attestations: list of signer-ids + signature blobs (optional).
  - approvals API: submitApproval(bundle_id, policy_hint, evidence_payload_ref, requested_ttl)
  - query: fetchApproval(bundle_id) -> full evidence or compact summary depending on requester auth and retention tier
  - retention tiers: ephemeral (30d, default for low-risk), standard (1y), e-discovery (7+ years, long-tail)
  - risk policy engine: evaluate(bundle) -> {low|medium|high} + reasons
  - sampling/aggregation: for low-risk events, store aggregated counters per resource with periodic snapshots; for high-risk keep full CEB

- Non-functional:
  - max ingestion burst per-customer: 1000 bundles/min (soft limit)
  - audit-read latency: <200ms for summary, <5s to retrieve full evidence from cold store
  - storage cost target: no more than 3x current baseline for medium-sized customers (50k events/day)
  - signatures: support KMS-backed signing (customer-managed keys) and Redwood service key fallback

Data format sketch (CEB):
- id: uuidv4
- created_at: iso8601
- actor: {id, display_name, role}
- resources: [string]
- diff_blob: base64(gzip(JSON Patch array))
- summary: short human sentence (auto-generated + editable)
- risk_score: float 0..1
- attestations: [signer_id::signature_b64]
- retention_tier: ephemeral|standard|ediscovery
(we will publish canonical JSON schema in spec doc)

Approval gate semantics (UX + API):
- UX: customer operator initiates a change -> bundling agent (on-prem or sidecar) collects related low-level events (iptables edits, route table changes, config commits) and creates a CEB. The CEB is presented in Console -> Approval -> Preview (shows summary + top 5 diffs), with a one-click approve + optional comment.
- API: approve(bundle_id, approver_id, policy_snapshot_id, ttl_override?) -> returns decision artifact (signed decision token)
- Decision token must include reference to policy version hashed, so later audits can tie a decision to a policy snapshot.

Signal & SLO instrumentation:
- Emit metrics: bundle_size_bytes, diff_count, actors_per_bundle, time_to_bundle, time_to_decision, risk_score_histogram
- Traces: create spans for agent->platform handoff, policy-eval, signature-generation
- Alerts to create: approval-burst (>1000 approvals in 5m), repeated-approve-loop (same approver signing identical diffs 10x in 1h), retention-eviction-failure (failed to move to cold-store)

Retention tradeoffs and cost model (rough):
- Example customer: 50k low-risk events/day grouped into 10k bundles/day; average CEB summary 1KB, full evidence 6KB compressed.
- If we keep full evidence for 10% (high/medium), storage/day ~ 10k * 0.1 * 6KB = 6MB/day. With e-discovery retention (7y) this dominates.
- Mitigation: default low-risk are aggregated into daily snapshots (aggregate rows kept: resource_id -> count + last_seen + md5 of last diff). Full evidence truncated after 30d unless flagged.

Forensic use-cases (should be preserved):
- Legal e-discovery: must be able to map decision tokens to evidence stored at time-of-decision.
- Post-incident replay: ability to replay exact sequence of CEBs for a resource range with preserved timestamps and signers
- Compliance attestations: proof that a decision was made by a role with required privileges and that evidence existed at decision time

Operator & customer roles matrix (sketch):
- Customer Admin: request/approve low-risk, view summaries, cannot override e-discovery retention
- Operator (Redwood): can view anonymized evidence for support bundles with customer consent, can flag bundles for internal investigation
- Auditor: read-only, can request export of full evidence under e-discovery flow

Sample console flows (notes):
- Quick-approve (default for low-risk) -> one click -> signed token appears in UI -> requestor sees result immediately, evidence archived to standard tier
- Escalate -> open a canary: gate copies CEB to reviewers (A/B), if disagreement, escalate to human review queue

Open questions / risks (to discuss):
- How do we enforce customer-managed key signing without creating availability headaches? (KMS outages, HSM latency)
- What is the right heuristic for bundling vs per-event approval? (time-window vs logical-op grouping)
- Do we need to persist policy snapshots forever to validate decision tokens months later? Storage cost of policy history?
- Legal: can we guarantee chain-of-custody for cross-jurisdiction customers? Need legal review.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (6w): CEB schema + in-memory bundler prototype (sidecar) + unit tests. Deliverables: schema doc, bundler binary, integration test harness.
- M2 (10w): Policy evaluation microservice + risk model (simple heuristic) + approval API + console preview UI (read-only).
- M3 (8w): Signatures + KMS integration + retention tier plumbing + metrics + alerting.
- M4 (8w): Sampling/aggregation pipeline + e-discovery export tool + SRE runbook
- M5 (4w): Beta with 3 customers (mid/ent) + iterate on cost controls

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Onboarding beta customers: reduce full evidence storage by >= 60% compared to naive retention while preserving forensic recall >= 95% for high-risk incidents
- Approval noise reduction: reduce reviewer time-per-audit by 40% (survey-based metric)
- Latency: summary retrieval < 200ms 99th percentile; full evidence < 5s 95th percentile

Rollout considerations / customer comms:
- Clear defaults (ephemeral tier) and easy opt-in for stricter retention.
- Provide migration tool to retro-encode older events into CEBs for customers who want long tail e-discovery.
- Docs + sample legal language for customers who need to map Redwood decision tokens to internal compliance records.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Aisha] Draft canonical CEB JSON schema and post to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- [Miguel] Prototype bundler sidecar that watches iptables and /etc/network directory for changes (POC).
- [Priya] Draft policy evaluation heuristics and sample set of rules for low/medium/high classification.
- [Jinsoo] Cost model spreadsheet (sheet link to follow) and initial SLO/alert thresholds.

Notes-to-self / todos that can be noisy in doc: 
- Consider compact counterfactuals (store minimal preimage for reversible ops only).
- Revisit whether we should include full diff blobs inline or only store in object-store reference.
- Talk to legal about retention + cross-border export rules.

References & inspiration:
- similar idea: compacted logs in DB audit literature; client-side bundling in other infra projects
- existing Redwood private-deploy documents (many in this folder) — this doc aims to complement them by focusing on entropy/signal reduction rather than pure attestation.

If you have energy: please review M1 plan and comment where we should tighten definitions for "bundle" vs "transaction".

-- end of brain dump --
